title: A film recovers from a failed segment without the viewer acting
description: A failed segment, a wrong keyframe index and a failed burn-in each freeze the film mid-play today, because jellyfin-web drops the stream on a segment error after playback has begun. The owner asked (2026-11-12) for recovery without the viewer acting, for example falling back from copy to re-encode at the same position. Observe first how jellyfin-web and an ExoPlayer client react to a segment error.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed in the e2e tier, jellyfin-web 12.4 (its bundled hls.js 1.6.16) in Chromium, after playback has begun, given one segment answered 500, one answered 404, one with no first byte for over 10 s, and one whose connection closes mid-body: for each, how many times it asks again, whether it asks PlaybackInfo again, whether a dialog shows and whether the picture goes on. Recorded beside the other captures, with the scenario that reproduces it
The same four cases are recorded for one named ExoPlayer (Media3) version from its source, citing the file and line for each, and marked not observed

A copy whose keyframe index is found wrong goes on as a re-encode in jellyfin-web in the e2e tier, with no dialog, no request answered 400 or more, no request abandoned, and currentTime reaching 30 s past the bad point. This holds when the viewer reaches the bad segment and also when the job finds it while the viewer is still playing stored copy segments before it
The re-encode goes on at the viewer's position: currentTime never goes back by more than one 4 s segment (so never to 0 or the resume point) and never skips forward by more than 1 s
After the fallback the viewer keeps the audio track and the subtitle track they had chosen
Two viewers playing the same copy when its index is found wrong both go on as re-encodes, as in the third criterion
Each fallback from copy to re-encode is in the operator's log (item, source and reason) and in a metric that counts once per stream that falls back, not once per segment

A copy job that fails for a cause that is not the file's (the transcode store refusing a put, the source store cutting a read, its ffmpeg killed by a signal) is made again as a copy. Its keyframe index is kept and no re-encode starts (invariant 45)

A segment whose job failed for a cause that is not the file's (the same three causes) is made by a fresh job and answered to the request that was waiting on it, with no error status and within 10 s of the request when the job failed at its first segment. This holds for a re-encode, a copy and a job that burns in a subtitle
When two requests (two viewers, or two stream replicas) are both waiting on a job as it fails, they start one fresh job between them, not two. The check makes both requests wait before the failure

A recovered failure stays visible: the job is recorded failed with its cause and counted in jellyscale_transcode_jobs_ended_total{result="failed"}, and it refuses neither the spec's later segment requests nor its PlaybackInfo
A cause that persists starts at most 3 fresh jobs (maxRestarts) for one request. The request then gets the documented failure that names the cause (JS-107), never an endless series of jobs

A failure that is the file's (ffmpeg failing on the file's own data, or the input ending early as in invariant 40) starts no fresh job of the spec within failureMemory (30 s), as today. It is answered with the failure and refuses the spec
notes: Built 2026-11-17, partly in OpenCode after Claude Code's weekly limit: refine and check on Opus 5.5, spec, build and fix on Sonnet 5.5, verify on Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, re-review on Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. jellyfin-web 12.4 observed in the e2e tier (compat/captures/segment-errors-12.4.md): after playback has begun a 500 or 404 on a segment ends the stream with no dialog and no new PlaybackInfo, while a stalled or cut request is asked again; ExoPlayer (Media3 1.5.1) read from source, not observed (JS-075). A job that fails for a cause that is not the file's is made again for the waiting request, at most three times per spec within failureMemory across requests; only a store failure the Reader gave up on counts (store.InputWithFailure). A copy whose index is found wrong goes on as an x264 or x265 encode cut on the playlist's layout (dropped_keyframes, Spec.Recode), capped at 1080 lines, priced from a measurement, each segment led by its own init; OutputVersion 5. The lead settled three disputed checks (the rig's film size, the HEVC length measure, a PlaybackInfo jellyfin-web never sends). Not built: AV1 fallback (SVT-AV1 exists but no restart-safe AV1 encode), a fallback while Postgres is away.
